title: Remove a soldered power inductor with hot air
instruction: Use the hot-air handpiece to reflow and remove the power inductor from the clamped, unpowered circuit board without damaging its solder pads. Put the inductor in the metal tray, return the handpiece to its stand, and release both.
context: A board-rework operation in robot power-electronics prototyping: remove a faulty surface-mount inductor so it can be replaced without tearing the converter PCB pads. Both soldered terminations must be molten before extraction. This uses an unpowered mechanical rework coupon representing the accessible component and pads; electrical function is not evaluated. The unpowered coupon stays clamped throughout heating and removal.
setup: Calibrated bimanual YAM station, table z=0.7475 m, seed 0, zero jitter and both grippers open. A 5 kg, 120×100×30 mm aluminum base at (0.24,0,0.7625) m is fixed to the tabletop. Two fixed steel clamp jaws at x=0.207 and x=0.273 m hold the near edge of the board. A 28.5 mm post supports an unpowered 80x60x3 mm FR-4 board at (0.24,0,0.8075). A generic 13 g moulded power inductor starts at (0.24,0,0.8142). Its composite body is 15.2x16.2x9.8 mm. Two plated-copper underside terminals are 3.0x12.5x0.2 mm, centred at local (+/-5.3,0,-5.0) mm; overall height is 10.0 mm. Nominal body, pad width/length and 10.6 mm pad pitch follow the XAL1510 dimensional reference; terminal thickness is an approximation. Board lands are 3.18x13.2 mm on the same pitch, with two copper tracks to 3 mm test pads at board-local (+/-30,0) mm. Three small package proxies lie beside the rework site. The fixed solder bond has nominal cold fracture limits 20 N/0.08 Nm and permits component/PCB collision from creation. A generic 250 mm/180 g preheated hot-air handpiece starts at handle origin (0.30,-0.18,0.8875), axis (0,cos32deg,-sin32deg), in two steel U-rests. Handle diameter/length 24/90 mm; heater barrel 18/90 mm; nozzle 8/70 mm, with a nominal 3 mm exit. It is regulated and flowing. All four material nodes start at 25 C. A steel tray has clear X=[0.30,0.40], Y=[0.15,0.25], floor z=0.7575 and rim z=0.7975. Exact original geometry and materials are in assets/geometry.json. The physical counterpart uses removable thin heat-resistant finger covers; stock simulated finger geometry and nominal contact properties are retained.
scoring: Primary score 1.0 when the thermally released component is wholly inside the tray, the handpiece is returned within 18 mm of its starting handle origin, the net vertical sum of actual normal and tangential-friction contact on the two tool stands carries at least 90% of the handpiece weight, both are released/resting and both TCPs are more than 100 mm from both complete object bounding boxes, continuously for 1 s. Resting: linear speed <10 mm/s and angular speed <0.5 rad/s. The tray allows 10 micrometres of numerical tolerance. Score 0.5 for a released component with intact board pads currently displaced over 15 mm from its original board-relative site in any direction; otherwise 0. Board displacement of more than 1 mm from its fixed setup pose, cold native bond fracture, cold displacement over 2 mm or declared thermal damage permanently gives 0. A loose object currently more than 30 mm below the table gives 0; recovery is allowed if the board pads remain intact and the final conditions are met. Material rule: an 8x8 patch grid on each of six case faces samples actual visible exterior heating inside a 20-degree half-angle cone plus 1.5 mm exit radius, 10-45 mm downstream, with the axis downward by over 30 degrees. A convex face must face the nozzle; air does not pass through the core to hidden solder. Heated patch area drives its actual lateral case half, normalized by 74.48 mm2 and capped at 1. Its heating coefficient is fraction/6 s and ambient cooling is (1-fraction)/20 s, toward 350 C and 25 C respectively. Two underside solder nodes follow their case halves through a nominal 2 s conduction lag while the component remains within 2 mm of its site. Both must reach 217 C before the native solder constraint is disabled. A previously molten terminal that stays in contact with its board land solidifies below 217 C; any such terminal re-enables the cold native bond at the measured current contact pose. Contact uses actual terminal/land overlap of at least 0.01 mm2 within a nominal 0.3 mm solder bridge. Separation clears that terminal's wetted contact; cold separated surfaces do not rebond merely on return. Both solder nodes must be reheated to release again. Cold displacement is measured from the latest solidified relative pose. After separation, heating the removed case cannot heat the board; exposed original board pads heat/cool from directly visible air with 6 s/20 s constants, and the actual component core can occlude them. At least 1 s above 320 C at either solder node is nominal board damage; damaged pads turn red. No component pose or velocity is assigned. No particular scanning or extraction direction is required. A real trial grades separation, intact pads under magnification and pad-to-testpoint continuity, tray placement, released tool return and rest. Thermal rules are approximations, not separate hidden step-credit tests; electrical function and neighboring-component thermal response are not graded.
run_limit: 1,600 control steps (80 simulated seconds at 20 Hz)
reset_notes: Use a fresh simulator process. Restore the fixed base and clamped, unpowered coupon, intact pads and solder, four 25 °C thermal nodes, empty tray and handpiece on its stand. On a physical bench, use source fume extraction and clean heat-rated removable finger covers that isolate the shared grippers from flux and solder residue. See the physical procedure in assets/PROTOCOL.md.
fidelity: Native grasps, fixed board clamps and cold solder fracture. Visible case patches heat two case nodes, which conduct to two underside solder nodes. Both must melt before release. Continuously wetted solder can refreeze at its actual contact pose. Thermal and fracture constants are nominal. Air flow, solder flow, electronics, extraction and heat transfer through finger covers are abstracted.
scores: Dream-1 beta run: 0.00; scripted native-contact demo: 1.00
